description: The open-source AIOps and alert management platform

summary.one_liner: Keep is an open-source AIOps and alert management platform that consolidates, deduplicates, enriches, and routes alerts from many monitoring tools, with YAML-defined workflows.
summary.what_it_does: Keep provides a single UI for alerts and incidents from many monitoring sources. It offers alert deduplication, enrichment, filtering, and correlation. Integrations are described as bi-directional, covering observability tools, communication platforms, incident management, ticketing, container orchestration, databases, and queues. Users define declarative YAML workflows with triggers (alerts, incidents, schedule, or manual), steps for fetching or enriching data, and actions such as creating tickets or sending notifications. The README also mentions AI-powered correlation and summarization, using backends such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama. Deployment is described as on-premises or air-gapped, with Docker Compose as the suggested starting point.
use_cases: Deduplicate and correlate alerts from multiple monitoring tools
Route critical alerts to Slack, Teams, or PagerDuty by service
Automatically create Jira or GitHub tickets from alerts
Enrich alerts with context from scripts, SSH, or AI models
Run a single dashboard for alerts and incidents
Self-host alert management in air-gapped environments
how_to_run: Use Keep's Docker Compose setup (the README names this as the easiest way to start)
Other documented options: running locally, on Kubernetes, with Docker, on AWS ECS, or on OpenShift (the README links these guides but gives no commands)
notable: Workflows are declarative YAML, described as 'GitHub Actions for your monitoring tools'
Broad integration list spanning observability, paging, ticketing, chat, and databases
AI backends for enrichment and correlation (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Gemini and others)
Enterprise auth options named: SSO, SAML, OIDC, LDAP, with RBAC and ABAC
caveats: Enterprise features such as SSO, SAML, OIDC, LDAP, and RBAC/ABAC are listed in the README, but their availability by edition is not stated
The README points to external docs for the full integration list and setup guides rather than giving them in full
